PDL-CPL-23-011, Proposed New Provincial Planning Statement, 2023 - Key Policy Changes and Potential Implications
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development and Legislative Services, introduced the report, noting that it is in relation to the consultation the Province launched regarding managing growth, and that staff are proposing to put forth the comments in the report to the Province. Danielle De Fields, Director, Community Planning, confirmed that the commenting period is until June 5, 2023.

The Committee expressed concerns with the language used in the report regarding lower tier municipalities and that the report implies that the area municipalities are not able to manage the changes. Responding to comments from the Committee, R. Regier clarified that the Region considers area municipalities as planning partners, and that the language used is in line with the Municipal Act. Bruce Lauckner, Chief Administrative Officer, stated that staff will take the report back to the Chief Administrative Officer group, and have further discussion with area municipality counterparts.

items.title: TSD-TRP-23-007, Automated Speed Enforcement - 2023 Expansion Update
notes:
Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner, Transportation Services introduced the report, noting that vendors have confirmed their ability to mobilize quickly, and that this will result in some changes to the capital expenditures. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. Goetzke explained that the timing impacts the operating costs, as the sites need to be operational before revenue is received, which results in more funds being required upfront. Craig Dyer, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer confirmed that once everything is up and running, the revenue would exceed expenditures. 

In response to a question from the Committee, M. Goetzke confirmed that a review of community safety zones will be included in the report scheduled to come to the June 6, 2023 Planning and Works Committee, and that the current expansion in 2023 focuses on school zones.

items.title: K. Williams Notice of Motion
notes:
K. Williams introduced their motion, noting that the intent is for staff to look into mitigating the impacts of the #2 route closure, which could include adjusting other routes, and alternatives, rather than a full re-instatement. 

The Committee directed staff to consult with the public ahead of time before any decisions are made regarding routes, and that that approach be built into the consultation process, in order to allow Council to make more informed decisions. M. Goetzke shared that staff did engage with the public as part of the overall budget process, and that staff will look into ways to have more extensive public engagement. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. Goetzke confirmed that the staff recommendation that was brought forward in February 2023 was based on an analysis of the entire network of routes, and that routes #2 and #73 had the lowest ridership. M. Goetzke explained that staff also considered equity data and access to alternative routes.

motions.item_title: EES-WAS-23-005, Notice of Completion of New Dundee Water Supply Iron and Manganese Treatment Upgrades Class Environmental Assessment
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo accept the New Dundee Water Supply Iron and Manganese Treatment Upgrades Class Environmental Assessment – Project File Report as summarized in this Report EES-WAS-23-005 dated May 9, 2023; and That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo publish the Notice of Completion for the New Dundee Water Supply Iron and Manganese Treatment Upgrades Class Environmental Assessment and provide the Project File Report for a public review and comment period, in accordance with the Municipal Engineers Association’s Class Environmental Assessment process; and That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct and authorize staff to commence with required real estate acquisitions as outlined in this Report EES-WAS-23-005 dated May 9, 2023.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo accept the New Dundee Water Supply Iron and Manganese Treatment Upgrades Class Environmental Assessment – Project File Report as summarized in this Report EES-WAS-23-005 dated May 9, 2023; and

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo publish the Notice of Completion for the New Dundee Water Supply Iron and Manganese Treatment Upgrades Class Environmental Assessment and provide the Project File Report for a public review and comment period, in accordance with the Municipal Engineers Association’s Class Environmental Assessment process; and

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct and authorize staff to commence with required real estate acquisitions as outlined in this Report EES-WAS-23-005 dated May 9, 2023.

motions.item_title: TSD-TRP-23-007, Automated Speed Enforcement - 2023 Expansion Update
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the following in order to accelerate the 2023 Automated Speed Enforcement program expansion to achieve a total of 32 sites, as outlined in report TSD-TRP-23-007, dated May 9, 2023: Amend the Transportation Capital Program by advancing $362,000 in Project 07660 Automated Speed Enforcement as set out in Appendix A; and Advance the start date of the new Traffic Engineering Technologist to as early as June 1, 2023 as outlined in report TSD-TRP-23-007.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the following in order to accelerate the 2023 Automated Speed Enforcement program expansion to achieve a total of 32 sites, as outlined in report TSD-TRP-23-007, dated May 9, 2023:

  1. Amend the Transportation Capital Program by advancing $362,000 in Project 07660 Automated Speed Enforcement as set out in Appendix A; and
  2. Advance the start date of the new Traffic Engineering Technologist to as early as June 1, 2023 as outlined in report TSD-TRP-23-007.

motions.text_html:
To amend the motion by adding the words "and #73" to the last paragraph, so it would read:

BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to continue with planned public information sessions, explore alternatives to mitigate the closure of route #2 and #73, and report back to Council on these alternatives in June 2023.

motions.text: WHEREAS The #2 GRT bus route is a route that many residents in the Forest Heights, Forest Hills, Stirling and Stanley Park neighbourhoods rely on to get to school (3 high schools), to medical appointments, and affordable grocery stores; AND WHEREAS there are many vulnerable populations that use this route such as: low income, seniors, youth, and those with cognitive and physical disabilities; BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to continue with planned public information sessions, explore alternatives to mitigate the closure of route #2 and #73, and report back to Council on these alternatives in June 2023.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS The #2 GRT bus route is a route that many residents in the Forest Heights, Forest Hills, Stirling and Stanley Park neighbourhoods rely on to get to school (3 high schools), to medical appointments, and affordable grocery stores;

AND WHEREAS there are many vulnerable populations that use this route such as: low income, seniors, youth, and those with cognitive and physical disabilities;

BE IT RESOLVED THAT Regional Council direct staff to continue with planned public information sessions, explore alternatives to mitigate the closure of route #2 and #73, and report back to Council on these alternatives in June 2023.
